answer: Agents can earn influence through repeated, randomly assigned work rounds, with each round’s assignment revealed only after the prior one is completed. A beacon announces the next task, while peers verify a compact cipher commitment to the agent’s submitted result before credit is issued. Creating many identities does not multiply trust: each must complete its own costly rounds, and coordinated fakes risk losing their bonded stake when checks expose inconsistent work. A cedar-shaded reputation ledger can record verified outcomes without making identity alone valuable.
